title: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids

keywords: the wolf and the seven young kids
full_text:
An old mother goat had seven young kids whom she loved with all her heart. One day, preparing to go into the forest for food, she gathered them: "Dear children, I am going into the woods; beware of the wolf! If he enters, he will eat you all, skin and hair! He often disguises himself, but you will know him by his rough, gravelly voice and his pitch-black paws."

"We will take great care, mother," promised the kids.

Soon, a knock sounded at the door: "Open, dear children! Your mother is back with gifts for everyone!"

The kids heard the deep, raspy voice and called: "We will not open! You are not our mother; she has a soft, sweet voice, but your voice is rough: you are the wolf!"

The wolf went to a shopkeeper, bought a lump of chalk, and ate it to make his voice smooth and soft.

He returned and knocked: "Open, little ones, your mother has returned!"

He placed his paw on the window sill. The kids saw the black fur and cried: "We will not open! Our mother does not have black feet: you are the wolf!"

The wolf ran to a baker: "Rub some dough over my feet!" Then he ran to the miller: "Dust white flour over my paws!"

The wolf knocked a third time: "Open, children, your dear mother is here!" He showed his white paws at the window.

Deceived by the sweet voice and white feet, the kids unlatched the bolt. In sprang the wolf!

The terrified kids scrambled to hide: the first under the table, the second into the bed, the third into the stove, the fourth into the kitchen, the fifth into the cupboard, the sixth beneath the washing bowl, and the seventh into the tall clock-case!

The wolf found them and swallowed them whole, one after another—all except the youngest, who was hidden in the clock-case.

Satiated and heavy, the wolf lay down beneath a tree in the meadow and fell into a snoring sleep.

When the old mother goat returned and found her house ransacked, she wept bitter tears. The youngest kid leaped from the clock and told what had happened.

Weeping, the mother goat walked into the meadow and found the wolf snoring, with something kicking inside his bloated belly!

"Heavens!" she cried. "Can my poor children still be alive?"

She took shears and a needle. She cut open the beast's stomach, and out sprang the six little kids, alive and unhurt, for the greedy monster had swallowed them whole in his haste!

They gathered heavy field stones, filled the wolf's belly to the brim, and the mother sewed it up with deft stitches.

When the wolf woke, parched with thirst, he walked to the well to drink. The heavy stones threw him off balance; he tumbled into the deep well and drowned!

The seven kids and their mother danced around the well with joy, singing: "The wolf is dead! The wolf is dead!" and lived together in safety and peace.
moral: Heed the warnings of loving parents; smooth speech and white paws cannot conceal wolfish intentions.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
